name: Aspen Grove
description: Clonal colony intelligence forming the largest and oldest known organisms on Earth (Pando: 80,000 years, 6 million kg). Interconnected root networks share resources, coordinate stress responses, and enable synchronized leaf emergence across thousands of genetically identical stems. Fire adaptation sacrifices above-ground growth to protect the immortal root system, regenerating entire forests from below.

core_attributes.pattern: clonal colony coordination, root resource sharing, fire-resilient regeneration

scope.definition: Net photosynthetic carbon gain per unit water transpired (intrinsic water-use efficiency) of Populus tremuloides aspen clone compared to co-occurring non-clonal deciduous species at equivalent light levels.

evidence.source: Mitton & Grant (1996) 'Genetic variation and the natural history of quaking aspen', BioScience 46:25-31; Rogers et al. (2014) Pando aspen genetics and physiology study.
cross_domain_examples: clonal aspen: shared root system redistributes water and nutrients — individual tree WUE 0.88-0.95
Pando aspen clone (Utah): 80,000-year clone with 47,000 stems sharing single root network
mycorrhizal-connected forest: analogous shared resource distribution increasing individual carbon gain efficiency

scope.falsifiability: If aspen clone trees show no higher WUE than adjacent non-clonal trees of equivalent size in water-limited environments, shared root hydraulics provide no efficiency advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: Clonal WUE advantage is most pronounced during drought — shared root access reduces stomatal closure frequency. Individual tree efficiency varies by crown position and stem age.
